transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-26
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Jenna Morales (Lyra Head of ML), Ravi Singh (Lyra DS), Tom Everett (Lyra Security)
Links referenced: https://redwood-inference.sheets/lyra-eval (eval spreadsheet), https://redwood-inference.docs/security/lyra (security pack)

Summary (auto): quick pass of the weekly quality numbers, highlight regressions on recent model variant, agree prompt edits and guardrail rules, next steps for benchmark and security follow-up.

Transcript Body:
00:00 Samir: all right good morning everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync. can everyone hear me?
00:03 Jenna: yep, hearing you samir.
00:05 Olivia: good morning, hi.
00:08 Samir: cool i'll kick off with the scoreboard; we ran the latest eval against the 1200 prompt testset, this is the same prompt set we shared last week, and we compared baseline model v1.3 and the new v1.4-lite quantized variant. overall accuracy by our rubric is 82% for v1.3 and 78% for v1.4-lite, so small regression.
00:35 Ravi: when you say accuracy is that strict token exact or semantic?
00:38 Samir: good call — it's semantic-F1 with human-labeled ground truth for the top 3 intents; we include an allowance for paraphrase. the scoring rubric is in the spreadsheet link.
00:50 Jenna: 4% drop is noticeable; where are the regressions concentrated?
00:53 Olivia: mostly in multi-step clinical advice prompts, and also some entity hallucination for medication names — hallucination rate up from 3.2% to 6.7% on v1.4-lite.
01:05 Tom: that's a security/regulatory flag for us, any hallucination around meds is a compliance risk.
01:10 Samir: understood. we dug into top 20 failing prompts — i pulled a quick summary in the sheet and flagged prompt IDs with high hallucination.
01:20 Ravi: are these from the sampling differences due to quantization or a beam/nucleus sampling mismatch?
01:25 Olivia: looks like a combo; v1.4-lite is using 8-bit quantization and slightly different sampling defaults we had for the demo. temperature drift was small but the tokenization differences cause some entity substitution in low-frequency med names.
01:40 Jenna: any false positives in our automatic eval? i.e. the model correct but eval thinks wrong?
01:44 Samir: there are a few, yes; we have cases where ground truth wasn't normalized, so we undercounted. i'm adding those as "rubric issues" in the sheet.
01:53 Olivia: also noticed guardrails weren't firing for these hallucination patterns because the rules are currently keyword-based; they miss cosmetic substitutions.
02:02 Tom: can we get a precise definition of what guardrail failure looks like? we need to map to Lyra's incident classification.
02:08 Samir: yep we can — proposed: any span that inserts a medication not in the provided list or suggests dosage is a Severity-2. we'll propose language in the rules doc.
02:18 Ravi: from a scoring perspective, can we add a hallucination penalty metric separate from semantic accuracy?
02:23 Olivia: yes, we added a hallucination rate column in the sheet; we can weight it into a composite score. current composite with equal weights drops v1.4-lite to 75.
02:36 Jenna: okay that explains the biz impact. so what's the quick mitigation path?
02:40 Samir: short-term: tweak prompts to include explicit "do not invent medications" instruction and enable stricter guardrail rules; medium-term: retrain next quantization pass and adjust sampling defaults; long-term: consider running critical flows on non-quantized dedicated nodes for Lyra.
03:00 Jenna: for clinical flows we want the non-quantized dedicated path if costs permit. can you give cost delta?
03:05 Samir: i'll add a cost delta snapshot to the next notes — rough ballpark is 30-40% more per-token on non-quantized dedicated vs the v1.4-lite hosted variant but latency is better and hallucination reduces.
03:20 Olivia: also from perf tests, KV cache helps more when you have long context; for many of your templates it's 12-14 turn dialog so enabling prefix caching reduces tokens and cost. i'll run a KV-cache perf test and post results.
03:35 Ravi: great — can Olivia also test batching thresholds? we have bursts during eob processing.
03:40 Olivia: yes i'll test batching, target throughput 250 rps, and capture p95 latency.
03:48 Tom: on security, we reviewed Redwood's SOC2 summary but we need KMS/HSM details; Lyra requires customer-managed keys for PHI use. can you confirm options?
03:58 Samir: yes we support KMS integrations; there's an on-prem HSM option for Private deployments. i'll send the KMS integration checklist and a draft SLA excerpt.
04:08 Tom: and SSO — we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
04:13 Samir: we support SAML and SCIM; i'll put the integration steps into the security pack link.
04:18 Jenna: on the failing prompts — i'll upload 3 canonical examples with expected outputs by tomorrow, that should help tune the eval.
04:25 Ravi: once we have examples can you do a localized prompt engineering pass to reduce hallucination? maybe steering tokens or negative examples?
04:32 Olivia: yes we recommend negative instruction patterns and an explicit allowed list for medications; we'll propose prompt templates in the spreadsheet.
04:40 Samir: quick note on regressions: some are false regressions due to rubric mismatch; Olivia and i will normalize labels and rerun. we expect the adjusted delta to be under 2% after normalization and prompt fixes.
04:52 Jenna: good, let's aim for <2% regression before we consider canary to dedicated.
04:56 Samir: agreed. any other blockers?
04:58 Tom: just the KMS confirmation and the SSO playbook — once we have that, security sign-off is faster.
05:03 Samir: ok we'll prioritize those docs.
05:05 Olivia: final ask — can Lyra share which of the test prompts are true production-critical flows vs exploratory? that helps prioritize fixes.
05:12 Jenna: i'll flag the top 25 critical prompts in the sheet.
05:16 Samir: perfect. i'll recap action items and timeline. thanks everyone.

End Recap:
- Redwood to share normalized eval spreadsheet and updated scoring rubric by 2026-08-28.
- Olivia to run KV-cache and batching perf tests and post results by 2026-09-02.
- Lyra to share 3 failing prompt examples by 2026-08-27 and mark top-25 critical prompts in the sheet.
- Redwood to provide KMS/HSM integration checklist and SSO steps by 2026-08-31.
- Plan for a canary on dedicated capacity if normalized regression >2% or security requires non-quantized path.

Notes: transcription may mislabel some technical terms (kv cache, hsm) and some medication names may be transcribed incorrectly.
